canonical.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
canonical.sourceFilePath: 07.Stack and Queues/3. Monotonic Stack and Queue/08. Largest Rectangle in Histogram.cpp

narrative.title: The Shipping Container Skyline
narrative.scenario: A port stacks shipping containers in vertical columns of varying heights, all one unit wide. Customs needs the largest rectangle of contiguous clearance the skyline contains — the maximal box that fits under a run of columns without cutting through any container. Each column's best rectangle stretches between its nearest shorter neighbors on both sides.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array heights where heights[i] is the column height at position i.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the area of the largest rectangle fitting entirely under the histogram.

testCases.explanation: Columns 5 and 6 together form a 2-wide, 5-tall rectangle of area 10.
The full-width bar of height 2 gives 4, matching the single column of height 4.

starterCode.python:
def largest_rectangle_area(heights):
    # Single-pass stack of indices with heights in non-decreasing order.
    stack = []
    best = 0
    extended = heights + [0]  # sentinel flushes the stack at the end
    for i, h in enumerate(extended):
        start = i
        while stack and stack[-1][1] > h:
            idx, hgt = stack.pop()
            best = max(best, hgt * (i - idx))
            start = idx
        stack.append((start, h))
    return best

hintLevels: Level 1: Every bar wants to know how far it can spread before a shorter bar blocks each side.
Level 2: A stack of indices with non-decreasing heights pops when a shorter bar arrives, computing widths on the way out.
Level 3: A trailing zero (or explicit final flush) drains the stack so right boundaries are resolved for surviving bars too.
